records.title: Don Haggar wins South Dakota Public Utilities Commissioner seat
records.byline: Vanessa Carlson Bender, Sioux Falls Argus Leader
records.description: Between Republican Don Haggar and Democrat Frank Kloucek, South Dakota voters have decided on who will fill the open seat on the state Public Utilities Commission.

records.title: Nicole Uhre-Balk celebrates historic reelection, saying it’s an “honor” to serve District 32
records.description: In the South Dakota House of Representatives race, four candidates competed for two seats to represent District 32. Incumbents Nicole Uhre-Baulk (Democrat) and Steve Duffy (Republican) won their races.

records.title: South Dakota doubles down on citizenship requirement for voters with Constitutional Amendment J passage
records.byline: Shalom Baer Gee, Journal staff Madison Willis, Journal staff
records.description: South Dakota voters on Tuesday, Nov. 3, approved a constitutional amendment that adds language to the South Dakota Constitution barring non-citizens from voting in local and state elections.

records.title: Baxter 'excited and grateful' to be elected as South Dakota Secretary of State
records.description: Republican Heather Baxter won the election to become South Dakota’s Secretary of State, the top election official in South Dakota.

records.title: Helene Duhamel reflects on SD Senate race win, says she's 'thrilled' and 'truly humbled'
records.description: South Dakota State Sen. Helene Duhamel wins her fourth and final term after beating challenger Jeff Shelton in Tuesday's election.

records.title: Blanc, Fleming and Bartscher elected to represent District 35
records.description: Republican Greg Blanc ran unopposed for District 35’s lone state Senate seat.

records.title: Constitutional amendment roundup: Medicaid amendment, 60% vote threshold rejected; Voter citizenship, unclaimed property fund pass
records.description: During this election cycle, South Dakotans had four proposed constitutional amendments to consider — Medicaid expansion, voter eligibility, unclaimed property revenue, and the threshold for approving future constitutional changes.

records.title: Rapid City’s legislative delegation largely unchanged; Uhre-Balk retains seat, a first in over 3 decades for a Rapid City Democrat
records.description: Incumbents held onto their seats in the four legislative districts that span into or exist entirely within Rapid City. The roster of lawmakers headed to Pierre for the 2027 will largely look the same, with the exception of Republican David Johnson heading to the Senate to represent District 33 and two new republican legislators headed to represent District 35 in the house.

records.title: A Democratic wave and more takeaways from the US midterm elections
records.description: WASHINGTON — Democrats took control of Congress in Tuesday's U.S. midterm elections, making extraordinary gains deep in Republican territory with voters delivering a sharp rebuke to President Donald Trump and his agenda.

records.title: Police say ‘arrest forthcoming’ after Tesla crashes in storage lot
records.description: The Rapid City Police Department said the suspect driver has been identified and an arrest is forthcoming, after a Tesla crashed into several parked camper trailers in a Rapid City storage lot.

records.title: Becky Drury wins over her new home district, 'excited' to return to Pierre after 2-year hiatus
records.byline: Tanya Manus, Journal staff Shalom Baer Gee, Journal staff
records.description: Republican Becky Drury is headed back to Pierre. Drury won over District 34 in the Tuesday, Nov. 3, general election. It's a victory that comes after a move across town, appointed stint in the legislature, a 2024 primary loss by just four votes and a 2026 primary win with a 46-vote margin.

records.title: Incumbents Jensen and Massie win over District 33 in statehouse race
records.description: In the District 33 House race, incumbents Curt Massie and Phil Jensen won their races and will be headed back to Pierre for the 2027 session.

records.title: 'Thanks and kudos to the people:' Johnson wins District 33 senate seat for 3rd term
records.description: In the South Dakota Senate race for District 33, former state Sen. David Johnson (R) beat out Christopher Baumgartner (D) with 65% (6,427) of the vote, with Baumgartner garnering 35% (3,448), according to unofficial results.

records.title: Mike Derby reflects on 4th consecutive election to represent District 34 in the SD House
records.description: District 34 voters on Tuesday, Nov. 3, reelected incumbent Republican Mike Derby to represent them in the South Dakota House of Representatives for a fourth consecutive, and the seventh overall, term.

records.title: Howard 'ready to get back to work' after District 34 reelection to SD Senate
records.description: In the race for state senator in District 34, incumbent Republican Taffy Howard beat Democrat Michael Calabrese with 4,943 votes (52%), with Calabrese receiving 4,508 votes (48%), according to unofficial results.

records.title: Rapid City Council votes to move general public comment to end of meetings
records.description: After two residents expressed concerns over the Rapid City Council's consideration to move general public comment from the start of the meeting to the end, the council voted to approve the change — but not without back-and-forth discourse.

records.description: August 31, 1936 - November 4, 2026

records.title: Leland Maciejewski
records.description: Leland Maciejewski, 89, of Hot Springs, SD passed away November 3, 2026. Funeral Service 10 a.m., Thursday, November 12, 2026 at Mueller Center in Hot Springs. www.chamberlainmccolleys.com

records.description: August 14, 1943 - October 17, 2026

records.title: William Murphy
records.description: November 4, 1958 - November 5, 2026

records.title: Kathy Jo Pfeiffer
records.description: October 8, 1944 - November 4, 2026

records.title: Holiday food drive happening now to support Rapid City families
records.description: A holiday food drive is happening through Nov. 22 in Rapid City to provide Thanksgiving meals to local families.

records.title: Public law enforcement services move to Pennington County Justice Center
records.description: As of Thursday, Nov. 5, all public-facing law enforcement administrative services have moved to the new Pennington County Justice Center, located at 130 Kansas City Street in Rapid City.

records.title: Vehicle takes out fire hydrant, light pole in Omaha Street crash
records.description: The Rapid City Police Department responded to a car crash resulting in the destruction of a fire hydrant and light pole Thursday morning.

records.title: Some Pennington County voters received incorrect ballots, potentially impacting RCAS bond vote
records.description: It's unclear how many Pennington County voters received the wrong ballot in the general election on Tuesday, Nov. 3, but Pennington County Auditor Sabrina Green confirmed some did.

records.title: UPDATE: Police arrest armed suspect after woman shot in torso in north Rapid City alleyway
records.description: The Rapid City Police Department located and arrested 21-year-old Tesean Richards in relation to the Thursday, Nov. 5, shooting that left a woman hospitalized with serious injuries.

records.title: Scott Anderson sworn in as new Director of Parks & Rec Department after council approves appointment
records.description: The Rapid City Council approved Mayor Jason Salamun's appointment for Scott Anderson to step in as the new Director of the Parks and Recreation Department.

records.title: Green to stay on as Pennington County Auditor until Mulally takes over
records.description: Bringing ease to the county as it faced significant gaps in the office that oversees elections, Pennington Auditor Sabrina Green has rescinded her original resignation letter and will stay on until Auditor-elect Tina Mulally can take the role on Jan. 18, 2027. Two members of her team set to leave the office are also staying on.
